verses.1: And the word of the LORD was spoken to Jehoshaphat, son of Hananiah, at Baal-Hazor.
verses.2: For you have taken me up from the depths of the abyss. We will judge Israel by your words. You will go along the path of Jeroboam, and you will bring Israel to their downfall through their sins.
verses.3: I am leaving after the destruction of his house. I have given your house to you as a place of refuge, just like the house of Joram, son of Nebat.
verses.4: The dead man in the city will be eaten by dogs; the dead man in the field will be eaten by birds of the sky.
verses.5: And all the other words of Baasha, and what he did, his deeds, are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.6: And he lay down with his fathers. He was buried in his own desire. And his son Elah became king after him.
verses.7: And also, in the hands of Jehova’s son, the prophet, God’s words were delivered to Balaam and to his house. They were also delivered to all those who did evil deeds, in order to provoke God’s anger through their actions. They became like the house of Jeroboam. And they were punished for their evil deeds.
verses.8: In the year fourscore and six years, during the reign of Asa, king of Judah. Elah, son of Baasha, ruled over Israel for two years.
verses.9: And his servant Zimri, the singer who was half of the band, was also bound to him. He was forced to work in the house of Arsa, which was located on the roof.
verses.10: And Zimri came and killed him in the year 97 after Asa, king of Judah. He became king after him.
verses.11: And during his reign, when he sat on his throne, he destroyed every house in the city. He didn’t leave any survivors or relatives for them.
verses.12: And Zimri destroyed every house in Baal-Zur, according to what the LORD said through Yehu, the prophet.
verses.13: To all the sins committed in the past, and all those sins committed by those who led Israel astray, so that they would provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel.
verses.14: And all the words of these men, and everything they did, are written in the book of the days of Israel’s kings.
verses.15: In the year fourscore and seven, during the reign of Asa, king of Judah, Zimri ruled for seven days. The people obeyed him wholeheartedly.
verses.16: And the people who were in the camp heard this song. They also attacked the king. And on that day, all of Israel became kings and rulers over Israel, with Amri as their leader.
verses.17: And Amri and all of Israel, along with him, went up from Gibeon. They set up camp there.
verses.18: And it happened that, when the city was captured, he went into the king’s palace. He burned down the king’s house with fire, and the king died.
verses.19: For his sins he committed evil deeds before the eyes of the LORD. He followed in the ways of Jeroboam, and through his sins, he led Israel astray.
verses.20: And the additional songs and poems that were written down are not recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.21: Then the people of Israel will be divided into two groups. One group will follow the plan established by Gibeah, and the other group will follow Amram.
verses.22: And the people strengthened themselves, along with Amri. They also strengthened themselves after Tivni, son of Gint. But Tivni died, and Amri became king.
verses.23: In the thirty-first year of King Asa of Judah, Amri became king over Israel. He ruled for twelve years. Then Amri was replaced by six other kings.
verses.24: And he built the mountain Shomeron, with its gates made of gold. He also named the city after the mountain’s guardian.
verses.25: And Amri did evil in the eyes of Jehovah. He was worse than all those who came before him.
verses.26: And Joram, son of Nebat, went forth on all paths. In his sins, he led Israel astray, thereby provoking the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.27: And the additional words of Amri, which he did, and his reigns, which he established, are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.28: And Amri lay down with his fathers. He was buried in Shemron. And Ahaz became his king after him.
verses.29: And Ahaziah son of Amaziah ruled over Israel for thirty-seven years, during the reign of Asa, king of Judah. Ahaziah son of Amaziah ruled over Israel in Samaria for forty-two years.
verses.30: And Ahaziah, son of Amri, did evil in the eyes of the LORD, in all that he did before.
verses.31: And Hananiah became a priest in the days of Joram, son of Nebat. He took a wife from the family of Etbaal, king of Sidon. She became his wife, and they lived together.
verses.32: And he built a shrine for the owner of the house that was built in Shomron.
verses.33: And Ahaz did what was wrong. Ahaz became known as a man who provoked Yahweh, the God of Israel, among all the kings of Israel who had lived before him.
verses.34: In those days, Hiyael built the Temple of God in Avirim. He established it there. When his son was young, he set up its doors according to what God said, as recorded by Joshua ben Nun.
